camera.motion: static (uniform blue sky, no background features; nothing to pan against, birds move at constant pixel steps so no sign of camera motion)
camera.perspective: none visible; 2D scene, both birds fly on the same horizontal line (y ~552-554) in a plane facing the camera; seen from below (ventral view)

objects.name: eagle
objects.description: large bald-eagle-like raptor: dark brown body and wings, white head with pale/yellow beak, white fanned tail; the LARGER bird, in front at start, flies faster
objects.heading: flies right-to-left (-x), head pointing left, body axis horizontal

body_length_px.note: beak tip to tail end, horizontal extent, constant (frames 2-14)

wingspan_px.note: vertical extent of mask (wingtip to wingtip, flapping); per-frame in track

objects.name: crow
objects.description: smaller all-black bird (crow/raven-like), black beak, wedge tail; the SMALLER bird, starts just behind (right of) the eagle and partly hidden by the eagle's tail in frames 0-1, flies slower
objects.heading: flies right-to-left (-x), head pointing left, body axis horizontal

body_length_px.note: beak tip to tail end, horizontal extent, constant (frames 2-24)

wingspan_px.note: vertical extent of mask; flap cycle ~9 frames (maxima f3, f12, f21; minima f6, f15, f24)

reference_point: x = cx_bbox (mid-point between beak tip and tail end, horizontal extent is constant so it is a stable body point), y = body line (eagle ~554.2, crow ~552.4; mean of head_y/tail_y for eagle, tail_y for crow). cx_centroid/cy_centroid also given but y-centroid is biased by wing shape during flapping.

events.what: first frame; frames 0 and 1 are identical (birds not yet moved). Birds overlapping: eagle tail end x=1762 over crow head (crow right/tail end x=1826)
start of motion: from frame 1 to 2 both birds already move at their steady per-frame step (no visible acceleration phase)
birds separate (two distinct masks from here on)
eagle reaches left edge (partly out), last frame visible
crow reaches left edge (partly out), last frame visible

motion_observation_px.eagle_step_px_per_frame: tail end x steps 119-120 every frame, frames 1->14 (mean 119.69 = (1762-206)/13); y constant
motion_observation_px.crow_step_px_per_frame: tail end x steps 73-74 every frame, frames 1->24 (mean 73.26 = (1826-141)/23); y constant
